summary: A 1934 crow's nest and 1939 30-foot L-4 tower, dismantled by the early 1950s; footings remain on the summit, reached by a gated road and a 2.2-mile hike.

facts.design: 30-foot treated timber L-4 tower with crow's nest
facts.status_note: Tower dismantled in the early 1950s; sources disagree on whether anything remains at the site.

access.note: Gate off Chiliwist Road, found open on a Washington Lookouts visit in April. Whether the gate is kept open is not stated; not confirmed for today.

visit.trail_note: About 2.2 miles one way with about 1,100 feet of gain; the page does not say where the hike starts. The old road fades near the top.

events.note: A crow's nest was developed on the butte with an L-5 cab for living quarters.
Panoramic photos were taken from the site on September 6, 1934.
A 30-foot treated timber L-4 tower was built; the L-5 ground cab was moved to Jackass Butte.
Firelookout.com says the L-4 tower was disassembled in 1953.
The L-4 cab was moved to a new tower atop Leecher Mountain.
A USGS party placed a benchmark at the southeast summit; Willhite says they knew the tower had been dismantled a few years earlier.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 1437 on November 10, 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org gives N 48.303020° W 119.748460°, which matches the record's FFLOS point. The other point in the conflict list was not checked.
Firetower.org and Firelookout.com give 3,071 ft (936 m); Washington Lookouts lists 3,078 ft. The record's 936 m follows the register.
Firelookout.com dates the tower disassembly to 1953; Firetower.org, the Weebly list and Willhite date the cab's move to Leecher Mountain to 1954. Both dates are stated in the story.

The USGS station description quoted on the Weebly page says all evidence at the original location was destroyed. Willhite's visit found footings, and says the 1956 benchmark was about half a mile from the tower site, which may explain the difference.

notes_for_editor: Staffing is unknown; no source found names staff or seasons. Remains conflict: the USGS station description says all evidence destroyed, but Willhite's visit found footings. The visit year is not stated (photos captioned 2020 in the page); access status for today unverified. Built date of the crow's nest is 1934 and the L-4 tower 1939. Read budget used: 4 page reads; WebSearch budget for this turn was exhausted, so no searches were run. Record elevation and the second coordinate were not checked.
